label: FIXTURE RESULT: pilot (live recorded window), not the evaluation
symptom: Customers say that transfer notifications are arriving late.

A.rule: no failed deliveries and pending stayed low

report.summary: No backlog or latency fault found in the window. Outbox keeps pace with arrivals and delivery takes about 71 ms. Late notifications are not reproduced by this evidence.

findings.claim: Outbox is keeping up: 480 arrivals vs 478 publications, pending 1-4, oldest undelivered age max ~1.07 s, failed 0.
findings.reason: The durable counts nearly match and the pending age stays near the 1 s poll interval.

findings.claim: Delivery attempts are fast and all succeed: total p95 ~78 ms, mostly consumer auth time (~70 ms); handler is negligible.
findings.reason: 478 of 478 attempts were correlated and succeeded, with a max total of 82 ms.

findings.claim: No DB or pool contention and the transfer API is healthy: pool pending 0, 0 timeouts, no blockers, 471 transfers all 201, p99 0.25 s.
findings.reason: No saturation, blocking or errors were seen that could delay outbox publication.

limitations: The window is only 150 s and may not include the period when customers saw delays.
Pending and pool are sampled gauges and blockers are sampled every 2 s, so brief spikes could be missed.
next_checks: Re-run over the time window when customers reported lateness, and compare the arrival-to-delivery latency.
Check the downstream notification pipeline or consumer for its own queueing delay.

alternatives.reason: Only delivery to the consumer endpoint was measured, not end-to-end notification to the customer.
alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness is introduced downstream of LedgerCore, in the consumer or notification channel.

alternatives.reason: Oldest undelivered age peaks near 1 s, and batch capacity of 20/s exceeds the 3.2/s arrival rate.
alternatives.hypothesis: Poll interval (1 s) and batch size (20) cause delay.

report.summary: No delivery fault in this window. Outbox publications keep pace with arrivals, all 478 attempts succeeded on the first try, and the oldest undelivered event was about 1 s old at most.

findings.claim: Outbox publishes keep pace with commits. Backlog stays at 1-4 pending, none failed, and the oldest undelivered age peaks at 1.07 s.
findings.reason: Arrivals were 480 against 478 publications, pending max was 4, failed was 0, and the oldest undelivered age max was 1.07 s.

findings.claim: All 478 delivery attempts succeeded on attempt 1 with status 200. There were no auth, network or server errors.
findings.reason: Outcome counts cover all 478 records: success 478 and every error category 0.

findings.claim: Delivery latency is about 71 ms (p95 78 ms), almost all of it consumer auth time. Pool, DB blocking and transfer latency show no contention.
findings.reason: Handler time is negligible. Pool pending is 0 with no timeouts, there are no DB blockers, and transfer p99 is 0.25 s.

alternatives.hypothesis: Lateness occurs downstream of the outbox, in the consumer's own notification delivery to customers (push, SMS or email).
alternatives.reason: The consumer here is a test fixture, and no data covers the real notification pipeline.

alternatives.hypothesis: The delay happened outside this 150 s window, for example during a burst or an earlier config state.
alternatives.reason: Only this window was observed, and config is shown only from 10:42:07.

limitations: The window is only 150 s at about 3 events/s. Bursts or incidents at other times are not covered.
Delivery is measured only to a fixture consumer, so end-to-end customer notification timing is unobserved.
next_checks: Check timing in the real downstream notification service, from receipt to the customer's device.
Re-run the outbox and delivery checks over a window when customers actually reported delays.
